data.narrative:
nTop, a Series C robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Bradley Rothenberg and Greg Schroy, has raised $138.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-proximate companies like Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Hadrian (Series D, $1.6B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised ($139M) as a proxy for valuation and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage step-ups, implies a valuation of $236M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. This wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer set, with some comparables at Series B and others at Series D.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $201M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $943M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median estimates reflects uncertainty around whether nTop commands a valuation premium or discount relative to the peer median. Key variables affecting the range include nTop's revenue scale relative to peers, customer concentration, and technology differentiation in the manufacturing software vertical.
